title: Teaching Students to Recognise and Report Physical, Sexual and Emotional Abuse in School Settings
what_it_is: Teaching Students to Recognise and Report Physical, Sexual and Emotional Abuse in School Settings

sections.label: Reporting concerns and seeking help
sections.summary: Students are taught to report concerns and seek help from trusted adults, and MOE reviews these programmes with stakeholders and agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Students are taught to report their concerns and seek help for their friends or themselves from trusted adults.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) reviews the effectiveness of these programmes regularly in consultation with stakeholders and other Government agencies, such as the Ministry of Social and Family Development, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Health.

sections.label: Recognising distress and peers
sections.summary: MOE teaches students to recognise signs of distress and to look out for their peers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In MOE, we teach our students to recognise signs of distress and the need to look out for their peers.

sections.label: Respect, help and reporting abuse
sections.summary: Students are taught their right to respect and help, that abuse victims should not blame themselves, and teachers are trained to detect distress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Students are also taught that they have the right to be treated with respect, to seek help and be taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Lessons remind our students that victims of sexual misconduct and abuse should not blame themselves nor feel guilty or ashamed about it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Through our lessons, students are also taught that they should not be fearful of reporting possible cases of sexual abuse.

In supporting students going through challenging situations and to help them feel that it is okay for them to seek help, our teachers and school counsellors are also there to train and also to engage students in a psychologically safe environment and on how to calibrate their approach accordingly, based on their understanding of the students' personal and familial circumstances.
Our teachers, as well, are constantly being reminded and trained to detect signs of distress in our students.
